context:
This is a small, surgical fix: remove the implicit write-then-fail
behavior from the missing-file branch so it degrades to a plain
pytest.fail with no side effect, matching how a content mismatch already
behaves (compare and fail, never auto-write). Optionally extract a small
helper (see w2) if it makes the new test cleaner, but a minimal patch of
the existing branch is acceptable if extraction adds more churn than
value.
description:
`tests/contracts/visualization/test_ascii_golden_output.py::test_golden_output`
(parametrized over all 15 ASCII chart builders) is meant to catch
unintended rendering changes by diffing against a stored golden file per
chart, with regeneration gated behind an explicit `--update-golden` CLI
flag (registered in `tests/contracts/visualization/conftest.py:9`).

The gate works correctly for the "intentional change, want to update"
path (lines 342-345: `if update_golden: ... write ... pytest.skip(...)`).
It does NOT work for the "golden file is simply missing" path
(lines 347-350):

    if not golden_path.exists():
        golden_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        golden_path.write_text(normalized, encoding="utf-8")
        pytest.fail(f"Golden file did not exist - created {golden_path}. Re-run to verify parity.")

This block writes the golden file unconditionally (without
`--update-golden`) and then fails once with a message telling the human
to re-run. On the very next run, the freshly-written file exists and the
test passes by construction - there was never an actual parity check.

Concretely, this means: if a golden fixture file under
`tests/fixtures/golden/ascii/` is accidentally deleted, renamed, or
gitignored, or if a rebase/merge drops it, CI fails ONCE (as a
`pytest.fail`, indistinguishable at a glance from a real mismatch), then
quietly self-heals and goes green on the next CI run or re-run - with
whatever the current (possibly buggy) rendering happened to produce
baked in as the new "golden" answer. Nobody has to run `--update-golden`
or review a diff for this to happen. This defeats the purpose of a golden
test, which is specifically to catch renders changing without human
review.

anti_patterns.dont: change the golden file format, comparison normalization (_normalize), or ChartOptions fixture values
anti_patterns.why: out of scope for this hygiene fix.

anti_patterns.dont: fold the missing-file case into the --update-golden branch's write path
anti_patterns.instead: only the NO-flag path needs to stop writing.
anti_patterns.why: --update-golden already handles 'file doesn't exist yet' correctly (it writes unconditionally)

anti_patterns.dont: make the missing-golden case regenerate automatically even with a warning
anti_patterns.instead: it must be a hard fail with zero file writes.
anti_patterns.why: that's the exact self-healing behavior being removed

preserves.behavior: All 15 existing golden files continue to compare successfully with no changes to their content.
Normal content-mismatch failures (line 353-355, existing golden differs from rendered output) are unchanged.
The --update-golden path (lines 342-345) continues to regenerate and pytest.skip for BOTH new and changed golden files - do not require running the test twice for a brand-new chart type.

verifications.description: All 15 existing golden-output tests still pass unchanged

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/contracts/visualization/ -k missing_golden -v
verifications.description: New test proves a missing golden file hard-fails without writing anything
verifications.expected: Test passes; asserts pytest.fail raised and no file created in the tmp golden dir

work_units.notes:
In `test_golden_output` (tests/contracts/visualization/test_ascii_golden_output.py:336-355),
change the `not golden_path.exists()` branch (lines 347-350) so it
does NOT create the file or write anything - it should behave like a
normal comparison failure:

    if not golden_path.exists():
        pytest.fail(
            f"Golden file missing: {golden_path}. If this chart is "
            f"new or the rendering intentionally changed, regenerate "
            f"with --update-golden and review the diff before "
            f"committing; do not let this test create it implicitly."
        )

Regeneration for a genuinely-missing (e.g. brand-new chart type)
golden file should go through the SAME `--update-golden` path used
for intentional changes (lines 342-345), which already
unconditionally writes+skips regardless of whether the file
previously existed - so no special-casing is needed there; only the
no-flag path (347-350) needs to stop self-writing.
work_units.summary: Make a missing golden file a hard failure that does not write anything

work_units.notes:
Add a test (in the same file, or a small standalone test module
under tests/contracts/visualization/) that:
  1. Points GOLDEN_DIR (or a monkeypatched copy of it) at a tmp_path
     with no golden file present for a given chart name.
  2. Runs the equivalent of `test_golden_output`'s body (or invokes
     it directly with `update_golden=False`) against that empty dir.
  3. Asserts `pytest.fail` is raised (e.g. via `pytest.raises` around
     the extracted comparison logic, or via `pytester`/subprocess if
     testing the actual collected test) AND that no file was created
     in the tmp golden dir afterward.
If `test_golden_output`'s body isn't easily unit-testable in
isolation (chart_name/golden_path/write logic is inlined), consider
factoring the compare-or-fail logic into a small helper function
(e.g. `_compare_or_fail(normalized, golden_path, update_golden)`)
that both `test_golden_output` and the new missing-file test can
call directly - this also makes w1's change easier to unit test
without spinning up a full chart builder.
work_units.summary: Add a test covering the missing-golden-file hard-fail path
